stem: In the Gospel of John (2:1–11), what does Jesus do at a wedding in Cana of Galilee, which John calls "the beginning of miracles" (his first sign)?
options: he heals a royal official's dying son
he turns water in stone jars into wine
he feeds a great crowd with five loaves
he gives sight to a man born blind
why: John 2:1–11: when the wine runs out, Jesus has six stone water jars filled, and the water becomes the best wine of the feast. John calls it the first of his signs; the official's son is the second (4:54).

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Juan (2:1–11), ¿qué hace Jesús en una boda en Caná de Galilea, que Juan llama "el principio de las señales" (su primera señal)?
options: sana al hijo moribundo de un funcionario real
convierte en vino el agua de unas tinajas
alimenta a una gran multitud con cinco panes
le da la vista a un hombre ciego de nacimiento
es.why: Juan 2:1–11: cuando se acaba el vino, Jesús hace llenar seis tinajas de piedra, y el agua se vuelve el mejor vino de la fiesta. Juan la llama la primera de sus señales; la del hijo del funcionario es la segunda (4:54).

stem: In the Gospel of John (20:11–18), who is weeping outside the empty tomb, mistakes the risen Jesus for the gardener, and knows him when he says her name, answering "Rabboni"?
options: Mary Magdalene
Mary of Bethany
Martha of Bethany
Mary, his mother
why: John 20:11–18: Mary Magdalene stays at the tomb, Jesus calls her "Mary," she answers "Rabboni" (teacher), and he sends her to tell the disciples. She is the first in John to see him risen.

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Juan (20:11–18), ¿quién llora afuera del sepulcro vacío, confunde a Jesús resucitado con el jardinero y lo reconoce cuando él dice su nombre, respondiendo "Rabboni"?
options: María Magdalena
María de Betania
Marta de Betania
María, su madre
es.why: Juan 20:11–18: María Magdalena se queda en el sepulcro, Jesús la llama "María", ella responde "Rabboni" (maestro), y él la envía a avisar a los discípulos. En Juan, ella es la primera en verlo resucitado.

stem: In the Gospel of John (19:30), Jesus's last words from the cross, "It is finished," are one Greek word, tetelestai, from telos (end, goal). What sense does the word carry?
options: my strength is gone, and I can do no more
the prophecy is not yet fulfilled, but will be
the work is accomplished, brought to its goal
the crowd's mockery has finally come to an end
why: John 19:28–30: John first says Jesus knew "all things were now accomplished," using the same verb. Tetelestai means completed, brought to its goal, not "I am done for."

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Juan (19:30), las últimas palabras de Jesús en la cruz, "Consumado es", son una sola palabra griega, tetelestai, de telos (fin, meta). ¿Qué sentido tiene esa palabra?
options: mis fuerzas se acabaron y ya no puedo más
la profecía aún no se cumple, pero se cumplirá
la obra está cumplida, llevada a su meta
las burlas de la gente por fin se terminaron
es.why: Juan 19:28–30: antes, Juan dice que Jesús sabía que "todo estaba ya consumado", con el mismo verbo. Tetelestai significa cumplido, llevado a su meta, no "estoy acabado".

stem: In the Gospel of John (13:34), Jesus calls "love one another" a new commandment, though Leviticus 19:18 already commands love of neighbor. What measure does the verse itself give for this love?
options: love as you love yourselves
love as Moses' law commands
love as you love your family
love as I have loved you
why: John 13:34: "A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you." The measure is no longer "as thyself" (Leviticus 19:18) but Jesus's own love, shown just before in the washing of feet.

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Juan (13:34), Jesús llama "ámense unos a otros" un mandamiento nuevo, aunque Levítico 19:18 ya manda amar al prójimo. ¿Qué medida da el versículo mismo para ese amor?
options: amar como se aman a sí mismos
amar como manda la ley de Moisés
amar como aman a su familia
amar como yo los he amado
es.why: Juan 13:34: "Un mandamiento nuevo les doy: que se amen unos a otros; como yo los he amado". La medida ya no es "como a ti mismo" (Levítico 19:18) sino el amor de Jesús, mostrado justo antes al lavar los pies.

stem: In the Gospel of John (11:23–26), Martha says she knows her brother Lazarus will rise "in the resurrection at the last day." What does Jesus's answer, "I am the resurrection, and the life," add to her belief?
options: the resurrection is present in him, not only at the last day
there is no rising at the last day, only a spiritual one
only those who saw him in the flesh would rise to new life
Lazarus would rise again, but only when this age ended
why: John 11:24–26: Martha speaks of a future rising; Jesus answers that the resurrection and the life are in him now, and whoever believes in him "shall never die." He then raises Lazarus.

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Juan (11:23–26), Marta dice que sabe que su hermano Lázaro resucitará "en la resurrección, en el día final". ¿Qué agrega a su fe la respuesta de Jesús, "Yo soy la resurrección y la vida"?
options: la resurrección está presente en él, no solo en el día final
no hay resurrección en el día final, solo una espiritual
solo los que lo vieron en persona resucitarían a nueva vida
Lázaro resucitaría, pero solo cuando terminara esta era
es.why: Juan 11:24–26: Marta habla de una resurrección futura; Jesús responde que la resurrección y la vida están en él ahora, y que quien cree en él "no morirá jamás". Luego resucita a Lázaro.

stem: After a fire, someone says a family's loss must be punishment for sin. In the Gospel of John (9:1–3), the disciples ask the same kind of question about a man blind from birth. How does Jesus answer it?
options: the man himself sinned, before he was even born
his parents sinned, and their child bears the cost
neither this man nor his parents sinned to cause it
the cause is hidden, and it is wrong to ask about it
why: John 9:2–3: asked "who did sin, this man, or his parents," Jesus answers "Neither," and turns from blame to the works of God, then heals the man at the pool of Siloam.

es.stem: Después de un incendio, alguien dice que la pérdida de una familia debe ser castigo por algún pecado. En el Evangelio de Juan (9:1–3), los discípulos hacen esa misma pregunta sobre un hombre ciego de nacimiento. ¿Cómo responde Jesús?
options: el hombre mismo pecó, antes incluso de nacer
pecaron sus padres, y el hijo carga con eso
ni él ni sus padres pecaron para causarlo
la causa es oculta, y está mal preguntar por ella
es.why: Juan 9:2–3: cuando le preguntan "¿quién pecó, este o sus padres?", Jesús responde "Ni uno ni otro", pasa de la culpa a las obras de Dios y luego sana al hombre en el estanque de Siloé.

stem: The Gospel of John opens, "In the beginning was the Word" (John 1:1–14). Who or what is the Word (Logos) in this passage, and how does the opening echo the book of Genesis?
why: John 1:1–3 says the Word was in the beginning, was with God and was God, and all things were made by him; 1:14 says the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us, meaning Jesus. "In the beginning" repeats Genesis 1:1, where God creates by speaking.

rubric.point: identifies the Word as Jesus, the one who "was made flesh and dwelt among us" (1:14). calling the Word only the Bible or only a teaching does not count.
says the Word existed in the beginning, was with God and was God, and/or that all things were made through him. "the Word is important" alone does not count.
links "in the beginning" to Genesis 1:1, or notes that in Genesis God creates by speaking ("God said, let there be light").
mentions the light that shines in the darkness, which the darkness has not overcome (1:5).

es.stem: El Evangelio de Juan comienza: "En el principio era el Verbo" (Juan 1:1–14). ¿Quién o qué es el Verbo (Logos) en este pasaje, y cómo hace eco este comienzo del libro del Génesis?
es.why: Juan 1:1–3 dice que el Verbo era en el principio, estaba con Dios y era Dios, y que todas las cosas fueron hechas por él; 1:14 dice que el Verbo se hizo carne y habitó entre nosotros, es decir, Jesús. "En el principio" repite Génesis 1:1, donde Dios crea hablando.

stem: In the Gospel of John (21:15–17), the risen Jesus asks Simon Peter three times, "Lovest thou me?" What does he tell Peter to do each time, and how does the threefold question connect to what Peter did earlier in John's story?
why: John 21:15–17: each time Peter says he loves him, Jesus answers "Feed my lambs" or "Feed my sheep." Three questions by a charcoal fire answer Peter's three denials by a charcoal fire in the high priest's courtyard (18:15–27).

rubric.point: says Jesus gives Peter a task: feed or tend his lambs/sheep (care for his followers). only "Jesus forgives him" with no task does not count for this point.
links the three questions to Peter's three denials of Jesus on the night of the arrest. linking it to Judas's betrayal does not count.
calls it a restoring or reinstating of Peter, or notes that both scenes happen at a charcoal fire.
mentions that Jesus then foretells the kind of death Peter would die (21:18–19).

es.stem: En el Evangelio de Juan (21:15–17), Jesús resucitado le pregunta tres veces a Simón Pedro: "¿Me amas?". ¿Qué le pide hacer a Pedro cada vez, y cómo se conecta la triple pregunta con lo que Pedro hizo antes en el relato de Juan?
es.why: Juan 21:15–17: cada vez que Pedro dice que lo ama, Jesús responde "Apacienta mis corderos" o "Apacienta mis ovejas". Tres preguntas junto a unas brasas responden a las tres negaciones de Pedro junto a unas brasas en el patio del sumo sacerdote (18:15–27).
